notes:
Answered strictly from documented public biography of Emmanuel Jean-Michel Frederic Macron, b. 21 December 1977, Amiens, France. Sources: English Wikipedia (Emmanuel Macron; Jean-Michel Macron; Brigitte Macron), Britannica, France 24, CNN/PBS/Al Jazeera on 2024-2025 politics, The Conversation (2025 'survival mode' analysis), Ifop/Elabe polling summaries, HATVP wealth-declaration reporting (Yahoo Finance FR, AgoraVox, Off-Investigation), ABC News and Hudson Institute pieces on temperament citing biographers Sophie Pedder and William Drozdiak, and Anne Fulda's biography 'Emmanuel Macron, un jeune homme si parfait' as reported in JDD/AOL/Headline Magazine.

Part D omitted - this exercise forbade opening any reading. No astrological source of any kind was consulted.

Item-by-item reasoning and honest uncertainty:

A1/A2/A3 (birth time): genuinely undocumented outside astrological birth-data collections, which I was forbidden to consult. French civil birth records are not public and no news/biographical source I found states a clock time. All three answered 'unknown' rather than guessed.

A4/A5/A6/A7 (health): Macron's medical record is close to blank. The only documented episode is COVID-19, positive 17 December 2020, symptoms of fatigue, headache, dry cough, seven days of isolation at La Lanterne/Versailles with NO hospitalisation (Elysee statements, France 24, Euronews). No surgery, no chronic condition, no recurring body-area complaint is on record; hence none/none/none. Childhood health is simply not described in any biography I could reach, so A7 = unknown rather than a guess. A8 = 'no' on the basis that his childhood is well covered by biographers (Fulda, Pedder) with no reported life-threatening episode - an inference from silence, not a positive source.

A9 (grandparents' longevity): three of four are datable. Paternal grandfather Andre Macron 1920-2010 (90); paternal grandmother Jacqueline Macron 1922-1998 (76); maternal grandmother Germaine Nogues 'Manette' died April 2013 aged 96. Maternal grandfather Jean Nogues, a teacher from Bagneres-de-Bigorre, has no death date I could find. Mean of the three known = 87.3, so 80_90. 'mixed' is defensible given the 76-to-96 spread.

A10/A12 (parents): both alive; father Jean-Michel Macron (b. 30 June 1950), professor of neurology at the University of Picardy specialising in sleep disorders and epilepsy; mother Francoise Nogues, physician/medical adviser. Divorced 2010. Both answered 'distant but not hostile' on documented grounds: Jean-Michel told Anne Fulda that in the idealised-childhood narrative 'the parents, in this scheme, they disappear', and reported that Emmanuel sees his mother only three or four times a year - a distance Francoise is reported to find painful, saying she felt sidelined first by his closeness to Manette and then by his absorption into Brigitte's family. Against that: both parents appeared together at the 2017 inauguration and the father has campaigned alongside him. Not hostile, not close - 'distant' is the best fit. Both parents also actively opposed the Brigitte relationship in the 1990s (father asked her to stay away until Emmanuel turned 18; mother said 'I forbid you to see him until he turns 18'), though the mother later became close to her.

A11: the father rose to a professorial chair in neurology and the household was two-physician Amiens bourgeoisie throughout Emmanuel's childhood - 'prospered'. No documented reversal.

A13 (siblings): forced-choice conflict, flagged. He is the eldest SURVIVING of four: the parents' first child died in infancy/was stillborn before his birth (Wikipedia, Jean-Michel Macron article), then Emmanuel (1977), Laurent (1979, radiologist) and Estelle (1982, nephrologist). I chose 'lost' because the sibling death is the well-sourced, non-generic fact; his relations with Laurent and Estelle appear cordial and private but are attested only by low-quality SEO sources, so 'close' would be weakly sourced. If the scoring treats 'lost' as requiring a sibling he knew, 'close' is the alternative.

A14/A15 (education): Lycee la Providence, Amiens (Jesuit); moved to Lycee Henri-IV, Paris for his final school year and preparatory classes; failed the Ecole Normale Superieure entrance twice; DEA (master's) in philosophy at Paris Nanterre with a thesis on Machiavelli and Hegel; editorial assistant to Paul Ricoeur c.1999; Master of Public Affairs at Sciences Po (class of 2001); Ecole nationale d'administration, graduated 2004 with an internship at the French embassy in Nigeria. Postgraduate, no doctorate, never interrupted (the ENS failures redirected but did not break his studies).

A16/A17/A18 (work): salaried public-sector for most of his life (Inspection generale des finances 2004-2008, Elysee deputy secretary-general 2012-2014, Minister of the Economy 2014-2016, President from 2017) and salaried/partner private-sector at Rothschild & Cie 2008-2012. No own business, no trade. A17 = 'own': his career under an authority ended in resignation (August 2016 from Hollande's government), while the vehicle he created himself - En Marche, founded 6 April 2016 - carried him to the presidency in thirteen months and to re-election. A18 covers banking_finance (Rothschild M&A, IGF), maths_accounts (finance inspectorate, economic analysis), writing_media (published 'Revolution' 2016, editorial assistant to Ricoeur, an unfinished novel), counselling in the sense of advisory work (Attali Commission deputy rapporteur 2007, M&A adviser, presidential adviser), and design_art for the documented theatre and piano of his youth (he met Brigitte in her drama class and won a piano prize at the Amiens conservatoire). 'Law' deliberately excluded - his training is administrative/economic, not legal.

A19: 'above' is a judgement, not a fact - he reached the presidency at 39 having never previously held elected office, which most commentators (and his own critics) treat as recognition far outrunning accumulated record. 'about_right' is arguable.

A20/A33: he left Amiens for Paris in 1994 and has lived away ever since; all substantial earnings (Rothschild, ministerial and presidential salary, book royalties) were earned in Paris, far from his birthplace. Brief posting abroad only (Nigeria internship, 2002), so A33 = over5 rather than 'abroad'.

A21/A22/A23 (money): no documented betting, lottery or speculative trading - 'never'; his HATVP declarations list savings accounts, a life-assurance contract and book royalties, not a trading book. No documented inheritance or windfall - 'none'. Debt is documented and modest: the 2017 declaration showed 246,000 EUR owed to Credit Mutuel (2011 renovation loan) plus 53,000 EUR of civil-service reimbursement; by 2022, 122,515 EUR remained. Hence 'manageable'. Context on wealth: he earned roughly 3 million EUR at Rothschild 2008-2012 and became its youngest partner in December 2010, leading Nestle's ~9bn EUR acquisition of Pfizer's infant-nutrition arm in April 2012; the gap between those earnings and his declared 156,000 EUR patrimony in 2014 is a live journalistic controversy ('RothschildGate', Off-Investigation/Blast, 2025) with no legal finding. He declared ~550,000 EUR in 2022 and owns no real estate; the Le Touquet villa is Brigitte's.

A24-A29 (marriage/children): married Brigitte Trogneux (b. 13 April 1953, twenty-four years his senior, his drama teacher at La Providence when he was fifteen) on 20 October 2007, after her January 2006 divorce from Andre-Louis Auziere. The marriage is by all public accounts durable and close (nineteen years, constant joint appearances) - 'happy' - notwithstanding the sustained conspiracy-theory harassment directed at her, including the Macrons' 2025 US defamation suit against Candace Owens. He married at 29, unremarkable timing for a French man of his cohort, so 'on_time'; the anomaly is the age gap, not the date. No biological children ('none'), three stepchildren (Sebastien, Laurence and Tiphaine Auziere) and seven step-grandchildren; no documented fertility difficulty or child loss, so A29 = 'na'.

A30/B1 (temperament): documented characterisations converge on enormous self-confidence and belief he can 'charm or seduce just about anyone' (Drozdiak), charm 'wielded ruthlessly' (Pedder), a 'Jupiterian' self-conception, perceived arrogance and 'blinding ego', frenetic communication and micromanagement. His unguarded remarks are famous ('les gens qui ne sont rien', 'je traverse la rue', 'emmerder les non-vaccines') - hence outspoken. Bold: founding a party at 38 and dissolving parliament in 2024. Sociable and philosophical (philosophy degree, Ricoeur) and practical (finance inspector, banker). B1 = opt1 chiefly on 'outspoken, hasty in speech... drawn to philosophy'; the fit is imperfect because he plainly does NOT hate show, and opt2's 'calculating, quietly ambitious' also describes his concealed ambition under Hollande. Low-confidence forced choice.

A31: no documented depression, anxiety disorder or psychiatric treatment - 'no' on the evidence available, though absence of record for a serving head of state is weak evidence.

A32: 'strong'. He asked to be baptised Catholic at twelve, against a non-religious family; took a philosophy degree and worked with Paul Ricoeur; speaks publicly about the transcendent and about France's need for a spiritual dimension; but describes himself now as agnostic. 'central' would overstate it.

A34: 'brief' - sent by his parents to board at Lycee Henri-IV in Paris to separate him from Brigitte; plus seven days of COVID isolation in 2020. No custodial or hospital confinement.

A35 (turning points, all datable): 1994-09 move to Paris/Henri-IV; 2007-10 marriage; 2008-09 joined Rothschild & Cie; 2010-12 youngest partner at Rothschild; 2012-04 the Nestle-Pfizer deal that made his fortune; 2012-05 (15 May) Deputy Secretary-General of the Elysee; 2013-04 death of his grandmother Germaine 'Manette' Nogues, aged 96, in his arms - the single bereavement he has described as formative; 2014-08 (26 August) Minister of the Economy; 2016-08 (30 August) resignation from government, coded job_loss; 2017-05 elected President (7 May, inaugurated 14 May), youngest in French history at 39; 2022-04 re-elected with 58.5% (66% figure in one source is unreliable); 2024-06 dissolution of the National Assembly after the European-election defeat, coded 'other', which cost him his parliamentary majority. Not listed for lack of rows: founding En Marche 6 April 2016; being slapped in the face at Tain-l'Hermitage 8 June 2021; the 2018-2019 gilets jaunes crisis; the 2023 pension reform forced through under Article 49.3.

A36: 'much_worse'. The six years to mid-2023 contained real crises (gilets jaunes, COVID, pension riots) but he won re-election in them. Since mid-2023: European-election defeat and the June 2024 dissolution, a hung parliament, Barnier censured after the shortest premiership of the Fifth Republic (December 2024), Bayrou brought down after 270 days (September 2025), Lecornu resigning after 27 days and being reappointed within a week (October 2025), the 'Bloquons Tout' protests, and approval collapsing to a record 14-20% with opposition parties openly demanding he resign before April 2027.

B2: 'medium' - he is about 1.73 m, i.e. around average French male height, and slim rather than heavy; 'lean_tall' would overstate the height, so medium is the conservative pick. B3 'younger' - his youthfulness was the defining physical comment of his rise. B5 'hospital' is an inference, not a sourced fact: France in 1977 was near-universally hospital-birth and both parents were Amiens physicians; no source states the place of delivery.

B6: only two of the six rectification anchors exist for him. Both parents are alive with no reported major illness; he has had no surgery and no children. So: marriage October 2007, and first job 2004 (Inspection generale des finances on graduating from ENA).

Part C reasoning: C1 opt2 (debt has been unambiguously untroubled - one ordinary renovation loan, steadily repaid). C2 opt2 (no long-term illness of any kind on record). C3 opt1 (a genuinely rich intellectual/spiritual life - self-requested baptism, Ricoeur, philosophy - with no documented crisis of it). C4 opt1 by absence of any recorded ear/throat/voice problem across a career of near-continuous public speaking; low confidence because absence of record is weak. C5 opt1 (difficulty) on the specific documented distance from his mother and her stated pain at it, balanced against her being alive, well and publicly supportive - confidence deliberately low. C6 opt2 (Elysee, La Lanterne, the Le Touquet villa; a settled and comfortable domestic life). C7 opt2 - marriage brought him into the wealthy Trogneux chocolatier family and the Le Touquet property is his wife's; the only negative is a small ISF back-payment (~6,400 EUR for 2013-2014) after the villa was found undervalued. C8 opt1 - his father prospered, is alive at 76, and there has been no rupture, only distance. C9 opt1 - the enterprise he built himself (En Marche/Renaissance) won two presidential elections, even though it has since lost control of parliament. C10 opt1 at confidence 5 - ENA, the finance inspectorate, Rothschild partnership and a bestselling book make learned/professional work the most unambiguously successful area of his life. C11 opt1 - the only confinement is a boarding school that was academically excellent for him. C12 opt2 - reading 'immediate family' as his household, which is warm and well documented, while the strain sits with his parents (covered under C5/C8) and in the harassment campaign against his wife.
